headline: Council approves $269,295.81 for law department and asks mayor to sign request for state audit of legal costs.
summary: The money would come from the fiscal 2027 tax levy, and the request had been tabled at the last meeting. If the mayor signs the B paper, the state auditor would review the city's legal spending. Also approved: a $23,605,562 loan order for the Roberts Elementary School roof and heat pump project, with a possible MSBA grant. Also approved: $75,000 from the general stabilization fund for Medford High School building project legal costs.
decisions: Approved inviting residents to the ward two neighborhood meeting on December 2nd.
Referred the Tufts Park master plan request to the Public Works and Facilities Committee, with a report due in February.
Approved, as amended, the request for a master plan for the Oak Grove Cemetery expansion, with a check-in in February.
Approved $10,000 from the CPA Historic Preservation Reserve for the Unitarian Universalist Church roof, and $50,000 from the CPA Open Space Reserve for lighting contingency funds.
Approved a lease-purchase financing agreement, not to exceed five years, for a hybrid driver's education vehicle for Medford Public Schools.
Approved a $75,000 appropriation from the general stabilization fund for legal costs of the Medford High School building project.
Approved a $23,605,562 loan order and construction manager at risk method for the Roberts Elementary School roof and heat pump conversion project.
Approved a B paper asking the mayor to sign a request for a state auditor review of the city's legal spending.
Approved the $269,295.81 supplemental appropriation for the law department from the fiscal 2027 tax levy.
Did not adopt a small commercial tax exemption.
Did not adopt a residential tax exemption for this year.
Approved a minimum residential factor of 0.908635, the largest split tax rate allowed by law.
discussion: Law department funding: Members discussed the $269,295.81 request, legal bills paid from other department budgets, and a state audit that would need the mayor's signature.

Oak Grove Cemetery expansion: Public speakers asked for a master plan before any funding. They raised concerns about flat markers, a maintenance yard, and a second access road through conservation land. The presenter said the seven-acre design is an early concept, with public meetings planned.

Roberts Elementary School project: The project director said the total cost is $23,847,692, and work would run over two summers while the school stays open. The project would electrify heating and make the roof solar ready. MSBA participation is about 11.6 million.
Residential tax exemption: The assessor said deed review would take about 92 weeks. Members debated whether to adopt the exemption now, and it was not adopted this year.
Tufts Park master plan: Members said several Tufts Park projects need one coordinated plan, including youth sports fields. The request was referred to the Public Works and Facilities Committee.
